extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political theology, clergy, and scholars interested in biblical interpretation and church-state relations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on interpreting Scripture in relation to civil and ecclesiastical authority, sacramental practice, and doctrines (kingdom of God, soul immortality, purgatory). A chapter-length exposition of criteria for sound interpretation and for judging ecclesiastical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No contradiction between Laws of God and Christian Commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: There can therefore be no contradiction between the Laws of God, and the Laws of a Christian Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of conflict between civil law and divine law should be treated with caution: obedience to a lawful Christian sovereign does not thereby hinder belief or obedience to God. When apparent contradictions arise from sovereign actions, the proper judges are those appointed by the Church (or the sovereign as its representative), not private individuals. Example/anti-pattern: allowing private men to disobey the sovereign on the basis of isolated scriptural texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of private judgement in matters of obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall a private man Judge, when the question is of his own obedience? or shall any man Judge but he that is appointed thereto by the Church, that is, by the Civill Soveraign that representeth it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private adjudication of whether one may disobey the sovereign is rejected; judgments about obedience belong to constituted ecclesiastical authorities or the civil sovereign as the Church's representative. Anti-pattern: individual subjects deciding for themselves to resist or disobey on private interpretation grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obey an infidel sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Civill Soveraign is an Infidel, every one of his own Subjects that resisteth him, sinneth against the Laws of God...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects under an unbelieving ruler are still morally bound to obey civil authority; internal faith may remain private (as with Naaman), and risking life for it is a matter for expected heavenly reward, not public rebellion. Martyrdom is a personal choice, not a license to foment civil war. Anti-pattern: using private faith as justification for political resistance or rebellion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Scripture by scope, not by isolated words
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the bare Words, but the Scope of the writer that giveth the true light, by which any writing is to bee interpreted; and they that insist upon single Texts, without considering the main Designe, can derive no thing from them cleerly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive method: prioritize the author's overall purpose and harmony of Scripture over isolated or obscure verses. Avoid 'casting atomes of Scripture' (picking single texts) which obscures meaning. Anti-pattern: constructing doctrine from single, controverted texts without regard to context or whole scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid error from ignorance or abuse of Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: First, by abusing, and putting out the light of the Scriptures: For we erre, not knowing the Scriptures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One cause of spiritual darkness is poor knowledge or intentional misuse of Scripture; remedy by accurate reading and knowledge. Anti-pattern: declaiming doctrines based on misunderstood or misapplied scriptural passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject introduction of heathen daemonology into Christian doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondly, by introducing the Daemonology of the Heathen Poets, that is to say, their fabulous Doctrine concerning Daemons, which are but Idols, or Phantasms of the braine...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not import pagan fables (ghosts, fairies, phantasms) as if they were scriptural realities. Anti-pattern: treating mythic or poetic accounts as literal spiritual entities that contaminate Christian teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing vain Greek philosophy with Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirdly, by mixing with the Scripture divers reliques of the Religion, and much of the vain and erroneous Philosophy of the Greeks, especially of Aristotle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of uncritical incorporation of Greek philosophical categories into theological doctrine; such mixing generates confusion and error. Anti-pattern: adopting Aristotelian or other pagan metaphysical terms to define Christian mysteries without scriptural warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on false or uncertain traditions and fabricated history
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourthly, by mingling with both these, false, or uncertain Traditions, and fained, or uncertain History.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check traditions and historical claims for reliability before letting them shape doctrine or practice. Anti-pattern: building doctrines (e.g., rituals or beliefs) on dubious traditions or fabricated histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject identification of the present Church with the Kingdom of God
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest, and main abuse of Scripture... is the wresting of it, to prove that the Kingdome of God... is the present Church, or multitude of Christian men now living...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate the present, visible Church with the eschatological Kingdom of God. Demands: clear scriptural and historical argument if one is to claim the Church is Christ's earthly kingdom; beware political consequences (claims of universal ecclesiastical authority). Anti-pattern: grounding ecclesiastical supremacy claims in stretched scriptural proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize claims of papal vicarship and ecclesiastical supremacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequent to this claim... is the Doctrine, that it is necessary for a Christian King, to receive his Crown by a Bishop... and that every Bishop... taketh at his Consecration an oath of absolute Obedience to the Pope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate papal claims (e.g., Lateran Council assertions about deposing kings or absolving subjects) against scripture, history, and the political consequences they produce; be sceptical of doctrines that unduly free clergy from civil accountability. Anti-pattern: accepting papal political supremacy on the basis of strained scriptural allegory (two swords, luminaries, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question clerical claims to special revenue and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Clergy signifieth those, whose maintenance is that Revenue... The Pope therefore... claiming to himself and his subordinate Ministers, the like revenue... Tithes... have a long time been demanded, and taken of Christians, by Ecclesiastiques, Jure Divino.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims that tithes, tributes, or juridical exemptions are 'God's right'—compare historical practice and civic justice. Anti-pattern: treating clerical revenue and civil exemptions as divinely mandated without scrutiny (resulting in double tribute and social imbalance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish consecration (dedication) from conjuration/enchantment
rubrics_metrics.description: To Consecrate... is to Offer, Give, or Dedicate... and thereby to change, not the thing Consecrated, but onely the use of it, from being Profane and common, to be Holy... But when... the nature of the thing it selfe, is pretended to be changed, it is not Consecration, but either an extraordinary worke of God, or a vaine and impious Conjuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for sacramental language: consecration signifies change of use/setting, not a change of substance. Claims of transubstantiation or literal change of nature without perceptible evidence should be treated as conjuration or delusion. Example: Eucharistic transubstantiation criticized as treating priestly words like a charm. Anti-pattern: turning ritual formulas into charms that claim physical transformation contrary to sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat baptismal exorcisms and ritual charms skeptically
rubrics_metrics.description: In Baptisme... the Priest saith, 'I Conjure thee, thou Creature of Water...' ...the Priest blows thrice in the Childs face, and sayes, 'Goe out of him unclean Spirit...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial elements presented as exorcisms or conjurations (conjured water, conjured salt, repeated exorcisms on infants) are to be seen as incantation-like abuses rather than necessary aspects of legitimate consecration. Anti-pattern: systematic use of exorcistic language and gestures in ordinary sacraments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid charms in marriage, visitation, and consecration of places
rubrics_metrics.description: Other rites... are not exempt from Charms; in as much as there is in them the use of Enchanted Oyle, and Water, with the abuse of the Crosse...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rituals for marriage, extreme unction, visiting the sick, consecrating churches and churchyards should not depend on 'enchanted' substances or irrelevant magical formulas. Ceremonies must be appropriate to their purpose. Anti-pattern: employing oil/water as enchanted talismans or inserting irrelevant psalms/words as charms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret 'Eternal Life' and 'Everlasting Death' contextually and conditionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Another generall Error, is from the Misinterpretation of the words Eternall Life, Everlasting Death, and the Second Death... God created Adam in an estate of Living for Ever, which was conditionall...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand 'eternal life' as conditional (restored by Christ to the faithful) rather than as an automatic, natural immortality of all souls. Read obscure NT passages in light of the whole scriptural scope. Anti-pattern: reading passages as teaching universal natural immortality leading to doctrines of universal eternal life or eternal torments without judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace doctrines (purgatory, invocation, indulgences) to their interpretive roots
rubrics_metrics.description: This window it is, that gives entrance to the Dark Doctrine, first, of Eternall Torments; and afterwards of Purgatory... and to the Doctrine of Indulgences...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encountering doctrines like purgatory, invocation of saints, exorcism practices, or indulgences, examine whether these arise from misinterpretation, tradition, or profit motives rather than clear scriptural warrant. Anti-pattern: institutionalizing speculative or profitable practices lacking scriptural foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonies must be decent, significant, and conformable to the action
rubrics_metrics.description: the ceremonies, words, and gestures, be both decent, and significant, or at least conformable to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rites against precedent of scriptural/early-practice simplicity (e.g., Moses' anointing, Solomon's dedication) — rites should be appropriate, not grotesque additions (no needless exorcised water, no irrelevant spittle). Anti-pattern: adding processions, exorcisms, or theatrical gestures that have no relation to the substantive action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret prophetic or difficult texts by grammar and context (example: Mark 9:1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The words are (Marke 9.1.) 'Verily, I say unto you, that there be some of them that stand here, which shall not tast of death, till they have seene the Kingdome of God come with power.' ...the same difficulty is also in the place of St. Marke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve difficult passages by grammar, immediate context, parallel accounts, and likely referent events (e.g., relate Mark 9:1 to the Transfiguration vision) rather than producing doctrinal claims (e.g., that the Kingdom already begun). Anti-pattern: literalizing isolated prophetic sayings to assert theological positions that contradict broader teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject arbitrary allegorical readings to justify temporal power
rubrics_metrics.description: As for some other texts, to prove the Popes Power over civill Soveraignes... as that the two Swords... were the Spirituall and the Temporall Sword... and that of the two Luminaries, the greater signifies the Pope, and the lesser the King...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reading political or institutional meanings into biblical images in order to justify contemporary claims of authority. Such inferences are often arbitrary and serve political agendas rather than sound exegesis. Anti-pattern: deriving papal temporal supremacy from allegorical readings of scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the immortality of the soul as a question of grace, not proven as natural by scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove that the Soule separated from the Body liveth eternally... there are divers places, which at the first sight seem to serve the turn: but such, as when I compare them with... seem to mee much more subject to a divers interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming the soul's natural, independent immortality, weigh scriptural passages (e.g., Ecclesiastes, Job) that are ambiguous or better read to indicate that eternal continuance is by God's special grace. Anti-pattern: treating poetic or ambiguous texts as conclusive proof of natural immortality.
